$comment: `__SIZEOF_LONG_DOUBLE__` PREDEFINED, and equal to `sizeof(long double)` (D-C-SIZEOF-LONG-DOUBLE-NOT-PREDEFINED). The file stops at an `#error` when the macro is undefined and at a `_Static_assert` when it disagrees with the type; at run time a `long double` must survive a copy of exactly that many bytes (exit 11) and an array must stride by it (exit 12) — `main.c` lists the codes. The value is the FORMAT's: 16 on aarch64 Linux (binary128) and on x86_64 Linux (x87 in 16 bytes), 8 on Windows (binary64, the MSVC ABI) and Apple arm64. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-19, each reference separately: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 on x86_64 Linux and on aarch64 Linux (qemu) at -O0 and -O2; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 runs it to 42 at -O0 and -O2 (its `long double` is x87 in 16 bytes — consistent with itself, and NOT the value DSS's binary64 PE model states); clang compiles it (-c, -O0 and -O2) for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, arm64-apple-macos11 and x86_64-apple-macos11, predefining 8, 8 and 16. MSVC cl 19.51 predefines no `__SIZEOF_*` name and stops at the `#error` (C1189): the macro is the GNU extension gcc and clang share. ★ The `release` arm: the copied value comes from a `volatile`, so the optimized pipeline still moves the bytes.
